decisions.reason: Despite its original flagship role, two years without visible market presence suggest the firm has learned enough to judge that this citrus-specific crate is not earning a strong enough place in the portfolio relative to other reusable packaging projects.

A foldable large container is highly aligned with the firm's existing container engineering and customer base, so even with weak recent visibility management would still be inclined to retain and refine a platform product of this kind.

A stackable plastic crate sits very close to the firm's core reusable crate knowledge, making it a product the firm can continue to support and improve even if it is no longer prominently marketed on the website.

Rackable pallets remain central to the firm's pallet capabilities, so the firm would usually keep this medium-duty line unless internal sales evidence clearly showed that customer feedback could not be turned into a viable offering.

The spill-retention pallet is a more specialized adjacent niche, and after extended lack of visible market support the firm would likely reallocate resources to better-absorbed core pallet and container lines.

Although based on familiar pallet technology, this load-retainer variant appears not to have secured enough distinct market traction, so management would likely fold the learning into the broader pallet range and discontinue the standalone product.
